headline: Ivy gets a basket, a voice and a bell of her own
lede: Homebody's second neighbour came home from the market properly this shift: the gift basket is now physically set down at the kitchen with a low thunk, Ivy rings a three-note lilt that lands down instead of up, and the BONDS panel survives a phone screen. Along the way the pass found and fixed a real stranding bug — some seeds never showed Ivy at all, because her schedule could roll past her own window with nothing left to re-roll it.

notes.text: #2240 shipped (PR #2282, merge b7f7f07, prod-verified): set-down basket with hop+squash on the depth line and a distinct 150/95 Hz thunk; VISIT_TIMBRE data table (Fern keeps her two-bell, Ivy gets 587-988-740 + heavier basket steps); attract rings Ivy once, and only when her own schedule can no longer land; BONDS rows drawn from exported bondRows(s) so painter and probe cannot drift. peoplecheck 497/0 (new 17-gate section, winnable seeds byte-identical), browser drive 72/0, two mutants each kill exactly their promised gates.

Bonus honesty fix: Ivy's ring never got a chat bubble — the resident's 2.4 s conversation clock was a lifetime counter Fern always spent first. Claims now re-arm the clock per guest; the meters never noticed and keep ticking.

Two attract staging ideas were built and CUT in the same breath: a forced noon pull and a nudged stroll to Ivy's ring each tipped WINNABLE seed 7 — a seed that wins main by exactly §10 — out of the win. The economy that proves the game can be won outranks a demo beat; the lonely-resident nearest-visitor law already walks players to her honestly.

Pixel gates on pulsing gold must sample across pulse phases — one frame is a lottery. And when a browser leg goes red on a branch, run the same drive against origin/main first: this session's red leg was a base that predated #2276, not new code.
